_comment: Everything you can buy and eat. Edit freely -- this file is not overwritten by an update
unless you deploy with -FreshData.
hunger  how much of the stomach it fills, 0 to 1. A full meal is about 0.45.
wake    how much tiredness it takes off, 0 to 1. Caffeine only, and CAPPED in code:
it can carry you to just above the tired threshold and no further, so a
pocketful of energy drinks can never replace sleeping.
drink   true for anything you drink. Drinks give a SMALL hunger increase by design.
booze   how drunk one makes you, 0 to 1. The meter is capped at 1, so the fourth
beer does less than the first. Drink also makes tiredness come on faster
-- see [Drink] SleepMultiplier in the ini.
shop    false keeps it OFF shop counters and vending machines. For things only
one particular vendor sells -- a branded burger belongs at that door,
not on the shelf of every 24/7 in the state.
prop    what appears in your hand. EITHER one name or a LIST of candidates -- the
first that exists in your build wins, and the misses are named in the log.
A prop name is the easiest thing here to get slightly wrong and the failure
is invisible: the food still works, it just never appears in your hand.
seconds how long the eating animation runs.
vehicleSeconds  how long it runs IN A CAR. A drive-through combo is set to a
minute: you pick at it between junctions rather than gulping it.
combo   alternates the hand between the food and drinkProp every few seconds,
for anything that comes with a drink.
drinkProp  the cup, for a combo. Same single-or-list rule as prop.
Categories are the tabs across the top of the counter menu, in this order.
icon    which product shape shows in a shop. See tools/make_products.py.
tint    what colour to draw that shape, #rrggbb. The art is white.
desc    the line the shop shows. Where the character lives.
smoke   something you smoke rather than eat or drink.

items.name: Club Sandwich
items.desc: Cut into triangles by somebody who did not care.

items.name: Bleeder Burger
items.desc: Bleeds a bit. That is the name, and the experience.

items._note: The street cart burger. Its own item so the cart is not selling a restaurant's branded one, and so its price can be a cart's price.
items.name: Cart Burger
items.desc: Off a cart, off a griddle, off the boardwalk. Better than it has any right to be.

items.name: Hot Dog
items.desc: Ninety per cent mystery. Ten per cent mustard.

items.name: Meat Pie
items.desc: Meat is on the label. That is as far as the label goes.

items.name: Instant Noodles
items.desc: Add water and low expectations.

items._note: THE TACO FARMER, the walk-up hatch. Its own wall paints a seedling growing
items._note2: out of a taco shell and the board lists nine plates, so it is not a Taco Bomb
items._note3: and should not be selling one -- this was the generic taco until the sign
items._note4: turned out to have a name on it.
items.name: Taco Farmer Taco
items.desc: Grown, allegedly, rather than assembled.

items._note: The drive-through's own plate. Carne asada tops the board and a combo is what
items._note2: a drive-through sells, so this comes with a drink and eats slowly in a car.
items.name: Carne Asada Plate
items.desc: Carne asada, rice, beans and a cup the size of your forearm.

items.name: Taco Bomb Taco
items.desc: Branded, shrink-wrapped and faintly warm.

items._note: Bishop's Chicken. Sold at their door only, never off a shop shelf.
items.name: Old Yeller
items.desc: Bishop's finest. Named after a dog. Do not think about it.

items._note: La Vaca Loca's drive-through board: pastrami sandwich, fries and a med soda.
items._note2: One combo, so the soda's small caffeine lift comes with it.
items.name: Pastrami Combo
items.desc: Sandwich, fries and a med soda. The board says so.

items._note: Gabrielle's Market. One of these is on the board at a time.
items.name: Bagel
items.desc: A bread product with a hole in it. Charged accordingly.

items.name: Fresh Fruit
items.desc: Nobody has bought one of these in a while.

items.name: Deli Sandwich
items.desc: Cut properly, by somebody who did care.

items._note: Aguila Burrito. Plain spelling: the accented A is not worth risking in the
items._note2: game font, and the sign says it anyway.
items.name: Aguila Burrito
items.desc: Foil-wrapped and structurally ambitious.

items._note: Ring of Fire Chilli House. Filling, and the soda is not optional.
items.name: Ring of Fire Chilli
items.desc: Named Ring of Fire. They were not being coy.

items._note: Lucky Plucker. Sold at the door AND at the drive-through lane, so it is
items._note2: set up as a combo and given a minute at the wheel.
items.name: Lucky Plucker Box
items.desc: A box of chicken and one small regret.

items._note: Cosas Baratas. Both of these are painted on the shop wall.
items.name: Tin of Sardines
items.desc: Tinned fish, on a shelf, in the sun. Bargain.

items.name: CandyBox Bar
items.desc: Box of candy. The name did all the work it was going to.

items._note: Drink. booze is how drunk one makes you; the meter caps at 1, so the
items._note2: fourth beer does less than the first. Keep buying and you get there.
items.name: Pisswasser
items.desc: Pisswasser. The name is the review.

items.name: Logger Lager
items.desc: Logger. Chops down a man twice your size.

items.name: Mount Whiskey
items.desc: Mount Whiskey, $15.99. You get what you pay for.

items._note: The 24-hour Mexican and American diner. Breakfast is on 5 to 11 only;
items._note2: the plate is what you get the rest of the day and night.
items.name: Huevos Rancheros
items.desc: Two eggs, hash browns and a coffee. Served at a reasonable hour.

items.name: Diner Plate
items.desc: Whatever is on the flat top at this time of night.

items.name: Bottle of Wine
items.desc: Wine from a shop with a security grille. Bold choice.

items._note: Fowl Mouthed Fried Chicken. Distinct from Lucky Plucker: a bucket to share
items._note2: rather than a box, so it is bigger, dearer and takes longer to get through.
items.name: Fowl Mouthed Bucket
items.desc: A bucket. For one person. Nobody is judging.

items._note: Hearty Taco, 'Eat Your Heart Out'. A sit-down plate, not the street taco
items._note2: from the hatch -- bigger, dearer, and it comes with a drink.
items.name: Hearty Taco Plate
items.desc: Eat your heart out. Their words.

items._note: Attack-A-Taco. Its own wall says HEAVY SHELLS and CHOOSE SIDES, so that is
items._note2: what it sells -- a loaded plate, distinct from Hearty Taco's and from the
items._note3: street taco at the Vespucci hatch.
items.name: Heavy Shells
items.desc: Heavy shells, choose sides. A war has broken out in your mouth.

items.name: Bag of Crisps
items.desc: Mostly air, sold by weight.

items.name: Ego Chaser Bar
items.desc: For the man who has everything, including this.

items.name: Meteorite Bar
items.desc: The candy that kids and stoners love.

items.name: P&Q Bar
items.desc: Peace and quiet. Comes in a loud wrapper.

items.name: Beef Jerky
items.desc: Chewing it counts as exercise.

items.name: Apple
items.desc: A whole apple. Revolutionary.

items.name: eCola
items.desc: Deliciously infectious. Their slogan, not mine.

items.name: Sprunk
items.desc: Sprunk up your life. Sixty grams of sugar.

items.name: Raine Water
items.desc: Water, in a bottle, for money.

items.name: Bean Machine Coffee
items.desc: Bean Machine. Tastes like the inside of a thermos.

items.name: Junk Energy
items.desc: Legally a drink. Spiritually a dare.

items.name: Orang-O-Tang
items.desc: Contains no orangutan. Contains no orange either.

items.name: Redwood
items.desc: Ask your doctor if smoking is right for you.

items.name: Debonaire
items.desc: For the discerning gentleman who wants a cough with class.

items._note: The Coop, Cluckin' Bell's walk-up kiosk. Its board is burgers, shakes, donuts, Sludgie, ice cream, pizza and hot dogs.
items.name: Cluckin' Burger
items.desc: Chicken, they say. It has been in a fryer, that much is certain.

items.name: Milkshake
items.desc: Thick enough to stand a spoon in. The straw does not stand a chance.

items.name: Donut
items.desc: Pink icing, sprinkles, no further questions.

items.name: Sludgie
items.desc: Brain freeze, sold by the cup. Legally a drink.

items.name: Ice Cream
items.desc: Melting faster than you can eat it. That is the whole game.

items.name: Pizza Slice
items.desc: Reheated under a lamp since some point this morning.

items._note: Wok It Off, the China buffet. The window says ALL YOU CAN EAT FOR $20 and SPECIAL LUNCH MENU, so it sells exactly those two things and a couple of boxes to take away.
items.name: All You Can Eat
items.desc: Twenty dollars, no time limit, no dignity. You will not need dinner.

items.name: Special Lunch Menu
items.desc: The same food, before three, for less money. Nobody knows why.

items.name: Chow Mein Box
items.desc: Comes in a box with a little wire handle. Traditional.

items.name: Wonton Soup
items.desc: Mostly broth. Two wontons, if the ladle likes you.

items._note: For the shop whose windows say BANKRUPT and REPOSSESSION SALE. Sold nowhere else, because nowhere else has given up.
items.name: Dented Can
items.desc: Label long gone, big dent in the side. Could be peaches. Could be dog food.

items._note: Bean's Market. Groceries and supplies, so it sells the things a corner grocer sells and nobody else in this file does.
items.name: Tin of Beans
items.desc: From Bean's. It would have been rude not to.

items.name: Loaf of Bread
items.desc: Yesterday's, at today's price.

items.name: Carton of Milk
items.desc: Check the date. Go on. Check it.

items._note: Bean Machine. THE WAKE VALUES ARE THE POINT: this is the one shop on the list that sells the sleep meter rather than the hunger one, and an espresso is worth more of it than a night in a parked car is worth of nothing. It is not a substitute for sleeping -- the meter still falls from wherever the coffee left it -- it is an hour bought back.
items.name: Espresso
items.desc: Small, black, and rude about it. You will feel it in the teeth.

items.name: Latte
items.desc: Mostly milk, entirely expensive. There is a leaf drawn in it.

items.name: Almond Croissant
items.desc: Flakes everywhere. On you, on the table, on the man behind you.

items.name: Blueberry Muffin
items.desc: Cake, before midday, with a job title that makes it breakfast.

items._note: Downtown liquor.deli. The counter item, so the shop is not only booze -- its own sign says deli first and liquor second.
items.name: Foot-Long Sub
items.desc: A foot of it. Measured generously, by them, in their favour.

items._note: Chihuahua Hot Dogs. A shop rather than a cart, so it sells things the two street carts do not -- otherwise it is a third hot dog stand with a roof.
items.name: Chihuahua Dog
items.desc: The house dog. Small name, large object.

items.name: Chilli Cheese Dog
items.desc: Eaten leaning forward, always, by everyone.

items.name: Corn Dog
items.desc: On a stick, which makes it street food and therefore fine.

items._note: Pipe Down. THE PRICES ARE THE CHARACTER: this is the only shop on the list where one item costs more than a whole meal anywhere else, which is what a tobacconist on a good street is. Smoke items report in words rather than a hunger percentage -- see Eating.Report.
items.name: Cigar
items.desc: Hand rolled by somebody, somewhere, allegedly.

items.name: Pipe and Tobacco
items.desc: Buying this is a personality decision and you have made it.

items.name: Boiled Sweets
items.desc: Weighed out of a jar with a little brass scoop. Worth it for that alone.

items.name: Bag of Toffees
items.desc: One of these will pull a filling out. That is the deal you are making.

items._note: Ground & Pound. Its own window says FRESHLY MADE SANDWICHES and HOT DRINKS, so that is the entire range -- no snacks, no cans, nothing cold. The name is a boxing joke about coffee and the descriptions know it.
items.name: Freshly Made Sandwich
items.desc: Made in front of you, at the speed of somebody being watched.

items.name: Toasted Sandwich
items.desc: Pressed flat under something heavy. Ground, and then pounded.

items.name: Pot of Tea
items.desc: A whole pot, for one person, with a little strainer. Very civil.

items.name: Hot Chocolate
items.desc: More of a dessert than a drink, and nobody here is pretending otherwise.

items._note: Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts. PICK YOUR RING is on the window, so the shop sells rings by the ring and by the box. The Coop sells a donut too, but one is a kiosk afterthought and this is the whole business.
items.name: Glazed Ring
items.desc: Pick your ring. That is genuinely their slogan.

items.name: Sprinkle Ring
items.desc: The sprinkles do nothing for the flavour and everything for the decision.

items.name: Box of a Dozen
items.desc: For the office, obviously. Obviously for the office.

items.name: Cup of Coffee
items.desc: Filter, stewed, bottomless in spirit. It goes with the ring.

items._note: BITE! -- the window says WRAPS Fresh and the sign says it's big, so the shop sells big wraps and things that agree with them.
items.name: The Big One
items.desc: It's big. That is the entire brand and they are not wrong.

items.name: Fresh Wrap
items.desc: Salad, chicken, and a word about how fresh it is on every surface.

items.name: Smoothie
items.desc: Fruit, blended, priced as though that were difficult.

items._note: Pizza This... The Coop sells a slice off a kiosk board; this is the pizzeria, so it sells the things a pizzeria sells and the whole pizza is the largest single item in the catalogue.
items.name: Whole Pizza
items.desc: A whole one. To yourself. Nobody is here to judge, and yet.

items.name: New York Slice
items.desc: Folded lengthways, because that is how it is done and you know it.

items.name: Calzone
items.desc: A pizza that has folded in on itself. Relatable.

items.name: Garlic Bread
items.desc: Comes with the meal. Ordered separately anyway.

items._note: Noodle Exchange. Wok It Off is a buffet that sells volume; this is a noodle bar that sells dishes, so they share a cuisine and not one item.
items.name: Bowl of Ramen
items.desc: Egg, pork, and a broth somebody has clearly been simmering since Tuesday.

items.name: Pad Thai
items.desc: Peanuts on top, lime on the side, no notes.

items.name: Steamed Dumplings
items.desc: Eight of them. You will want twelve. Everybody wants twelve.

items.name: Bubble Tea
items.desc: Comes with a straw wide enough to be a weapon.

items._note: Cool Beans. The fourth place on this list that sells coffee, so it sells it COLD -- the name did the deciding. Bean Machine is hot and serious, Rusty Brown's is filter with a donut, Ground & Pound is a pot of tea, and this one has pavement tables and a frappe.
items.name: Cold Brew
items.desc: Steeped for a day and a night. Hits like a bag of hammers.

items.name: Iced Latte
items.desc: Ice, milk, and a rumour of espresso.

items.name: Frappe
items.desc: Coffee that has given up and become a milkshake. No shame in it.

items.name: Big Cookie
items.desc: The size of a coaster and still warm in the middle.

items._note: Limey's Juice & Smoothies. BITE! sells a smoothie as a side; this is a juice bar, so it sells juice and the smoothie is the indulgent end of the menu rather than the whole of it.
items.name: Fresh Orange Juice
items.desc: Squeezed in front of you, loudly, by a machine that has seen things.

items.name: Green Juice
items.desc: Kale, celery, and the distinct feeling of being told off.

items.name: Berry Smoothie
items.desc: Squeeze one out. Their slogan. On the window. Twice.

items.name: Wheatgrass Shot
items.desc: Tastes like a lawn. Works like a slap.

items._note: Food Market. A SUPERMARKET, not a corner grocer -- so it sells the shop rather than the snack. Bean's does a tin of beans; this does the whole trolley, and the prices and hunger values say which is which.
items.name: Bag of Groceries
items.desc: A proper shop. You will be eating out of this bag for a while.

items.name: Rotisserie Chicken
items.desc: Off the hot spinner by the door. The best thing in any supermarket.

items.name: Ready Meal
items.desc: Pierce film. Do not pierce film. Nobody has ever known which.

items.name: Bag of Produce
items.desc: Bought with the best intentions. Half of it will go off.

items._note: Mama's Grocery. THREE GROCERS NOW, and each sells a different thing: Bean's does tins and bread, Food Market does the weekly shop, and this one has a hot counter at the back with somebody's actual cooking on it.
items.name: Mama's Meatloaf
items.desc: Cut off the tray, weighed, wrapped in foil. Ask for the end piece.

items.name: Homemade Soup
items.desc: Ladled out of a pot that has never once been empty.

items.name: Slice of Apple Pie
items.desc: There is a whole one behind the counter and she will notice if you stare.

items.name: Pantry Basics
items.desc: Rice, oil, tinned tomatoes. The things you only notice when they run out.

items._note: The market kiosk. Its boards list burgers, pizza, hot dogs, ice cream, sundaes, soda, sludgies, coffee, candy, batteries and film -- so a broad shelf IS this shop's character rather than a failure to give it one.
items.name: Ice Cream Sundae
items.desc: Three scoops, sauce, a wafer stuck in at an angle. Correct.

items.name: Thick Shake
items.desc: From the machine with MILK SHAKES painted on it in two colours.

items._note: Crucial Fix Coffee House. THE FIFTH PLACE THAT SELLS COFFEE and it still does not overlap: Bean Machine is hot and serious, Rusty Brown's is filter with a ring, Ground & Pound pours a pot of tea, Cool Beans is cold, and this one is a Jamaican roast with patties and ginger beer.
items.name: Jamaican Roast
items.desc: Roasted since 1983 and they will tell you so while it pours.

items.name: Beef Patty
items.desc: Yellow pastry, serious filling. Hold it in the paper bag or lose a shirt.

items.name: Ginger Beer
items.desc: The proper cloudy kind. Takes the roof of your mouth off.

items.name: Rum Cake
items.desc: There is more rum in this than anybody admits at eleven in the morning.

items._note: Up-n-Atom's menu board is readable from the street, so these four are what
items._note2: it says, at this mod's prices rather than the board's 1980s ones.
items.name: Triple Burger
items.desc: Three patties. The middle one is there on trust.

items.name: Bacon Triple Cheese Melt
items.desc: Ten slices of cheese, and the board is proud of that.

items.name: French Fries
items.desc: Salt, mostly. Nobody is pretending otherwise.

items.name: Jumbo Shake
items.desc: Strawberry, chocolate or vanilla. Extra creamy, it insists.

items._note: Horny's sign says BURGERS and 'the beef with the bone'; the window adds menudo,
items._note2: eggs benedict and two chicken tacos. Mexican-American, so the shelf is both.
items.name: Bone-In Burger
items.desc: The beef with the bone. You are asked not to think about it too hard.

items.name: Bowl of Menudo
items.desc: Daily. Cures whatever last night did to you.

items.name: Two Chicken Tacos
items.desc: Two for the price the board has not changed in years.

items.name: Eggs Benedict
items.desc: Or hash browns. The window offers you the choice and means it.

items._note: SPITROASTERS MEAT HOUSE -- 'the Bigger the Beef the Bigger the Roasting'.
items.name: Spit-Roasted Beef
items.desc: Off the spit, onto the plate, no step in between worth mentioning.

items.name: Rack of Ribs
items.desc: Comes with a roll of paper towel and no cutlery.

items._note: The board by Jazz's door lists appetizers, entrees, salads and soups, desserts.
items.name: Seafood Linguine
items.desc: Off the entrees. The menu by the door has been there a while.

items.name: Chocolate Torte
items.desc: The word DESSERTS is bigger than the word JAZZ. They know.

items.name: Tasting Plate
items.desc: Small, arranged, and costs what a week of tacos costs.

items.name: Small Plates
items.desc: Three of them and you have had a starter.

items._note: LIBERTY STYLE PIZZA -- Guido's Take Out, open 24 hours, free delivery.
items.name: Liberty Style Slice
items.desc: Folded lengthways, which is apparently the whole difference.

items.name: Whole Liberty Pie
items.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, and free delivery he would rather you did not test.

items._note: HEAVENLY TACOS, and the wall next to it says MEXICAN AND AMERICAN.
items.name: Heavenly Taco
items.desc: Named optimistically. Not entirely without cause.

items.name: Mexican-American Combo
items.desc: Both halves of the sign, on one plate, at one price.

items._note: CHIDO! -- the awning says TAQUERIA MEXICANA under the name, so it is a
items._note2: taqueria and not another Taco Bomb. Its own menu, like every other named
items._note3: shop here: a generic taco sold under a specific sign reads as a shortcut.
items.name: Tacos al Pastor
items.desc: Three of them, off the spit, with the pineapple.

items.name: Quesadilla
items.desc: Folded, pressed, and hot enough to be a mistake.

items.name: Plato Chido
items.desc: Rice, beans and the thing you actually came for.

items.name: Horchata
items.desc: Cinnamon, rice and more sugar than either.

items._note: THE GRAIN OF TRUTH -- the band under the logo says ORGANIC FOOD MARKET
items._note2: and the whole shopfront is a wheat sheaf. Its own items, because a shop
items._note3: whose entire brand IS what it sells cannot be stocked out of the generic
items._note4: shelf without the joke going missing.
items.name: Ancient Grain Bowl
items.desc: Quinoa, kale, and a price that assumes you are sorry about something.

items.name: Wheatgrass Smoothie
items.desc: Tastes of a lawn. Sold as though that were the point.

items.name: Organic Veg Box
items.desc: Muddy, misshapen, and dearer for both.

items._note: THE DICKIES BAGELS & DELI -- the sign puts BAGELS above & DELI, so the
items._note2: bagel is the shop and the deli counter is the other half of it. Its own
items._note3: items for the same reason Bean Machine has its own: a named shop selling
items._note4: the generic bagel is the shortcut this file keeps refusing.
items.name: Bagel and Schmear
items.desc: Toasted unless you say otherwise, and they will ask.

items.name: The Reuben
items.desc: Stacked past the point of being a sandwich and held with a stick.

items.name: Baker's Dozen
items.desc: Thirteen. They count it out in front of you, every time.

items._note: WIGWAM. THE MENU IS PAINTED ON THE WINDOWS -- BISON BURGER, CRAZY HORSE
items._note2: SOUP, GERONIMO WINGS, RINGS OF FIRE -- and the board in the corner adds
items._note3: THE BIG CHIEF SPECIAL above the other four, so that is the combo and the
items._note4: rest are the parts of it. Nothing here is invented; it is all on the glass.
items.name: The Big Chief Special
items.desc: All four of the others, on one tray, for slightly less than four.

items.name: Bison Burger
items.desc: Leaner than beef and priced as though that were an achievement.

items.name: Crazy Horse Soup
items.desc: Nobody at the counter will say what is in it.

items.name: Geronimo Wings
items.desc: Ordered with confidence. Eaten with a stack of napkins.

items.name: Rings of Fire
items.desc: Onion rings, and the name is a warning rather than a flourish.

items._note: BITE!, Del Perro. The poster in THIS window is the Gut Buster -- ALL 8
items._note2: INCH MEAT STACKS ONLY $3.99 -- which the other two branches do not have
items._note3: up, so it goes on this shelf and not theirs. $3.99 rounds to 4: the file
items._note4: has no fractional prices and one cent is not worth inventing them for.
items.name: Gut Buster
items.desc: Eight inches of meat stack for four dollars. Somebody did the sums wrong.

items._note: LETTUCE BE -- VEGETARIAN CUISINE, on the sign, under a peace symbol. A
items._note2: SIT-DOWN RESTAURANT: white cloths, table lamps, a full room of covers, so
items._note3: it is priced with Haute rather than with the parade round the corner. NO
items._note4: MEAT ON THE SHELF, which is the one thing the sign actually promises.
items.name: Chef's Garden Plate
items.desc: Nine things on it. Four of them are described as a foam.

items.name: Harvest Bowl
items.desc: Filling, which surprises everybody who orders it to be polite.

items.name: Cold-Pressed Juice
items.desc: Pressed rather than squeezed, and the difference costs four dollars.

items._note: BURGER SHOT -- and like Taco Bomb it has been in this file the whole time
items._note2: with nowhere to buy it: the generic burger is called BLEEDER BURGER, which
items._note3: is theirs. So the Bleeder stays generic and goes on their shelf, and these
items._note4: three are the rest of the board.
items.name: Money Shot
items.desc: Double everything. The name was focus-grouped by nobody at all.

items.name: Heart Stopper
items.desc: Named by the legal department, who lost that argument.

items.name: Torpedo
items.desc: Long, and it does go off in your hands eventually.

items._note: GIOVANNI'S ITALIAN RESTAURANT, and the second line of the sign IS the
items._note2: menu: DELI PIZZA SANDWICHES SALADS. Four words, so four items, in that
items._note3: order -- the deli half is covered by the shared deli sandwich on the shelf
items._note4: rather than by a fifth of its own.
items.name: Giovanni's Pizza
items.desc: Whole. Nobody has ever managed one alone and several have tried.

items.name: Slice
items.desc: Folded lengthways at the door, which is the correct way.

items.name: Italian Sub
items.desc: Oil and vinegar whether or not you asked for them.

items.name: Antipasto Salad
items.desc: A salad in the sense that there is lettuce under all of it.

items._note: LES BIANCO, in Del Perro Plaza, two doors from Haute. Fine dining: no
items._note2: menu is legible from the street, so the shelf is a COURSE STRUCTURE rather
items._note3: than invented dishes -- primo and secondo is what the room is, and it says
items._note4: nothing the window does not. Priced with Haute, which it stands beside.
items.name: Primo
items.desc: The pasta course, and the one everybody says they came for.

items.name: Secondo
items.desc: Arrives under a cloche. The cloche is lifted for you.

items._note: SUMAC RESTAURANT -- the name is the spice, and the front is bougainvillea
items._note2: over a pergola, so it is read as Mediterranean. Same rule as Les Bianco:
items._note3: no menu is visible from the street, so the shelf is the SHAPE of the meal
items._note4: rather than dishes made up to fill it.
items.name: Mezze Plate
items.desc: Eight small bowls. You will be full before the food arrives.

items.name: Mixed Grill
items.desc: Brought to the table still going, which is most of the price.

items.name: Mint Tea
items.desc: Poured from a height, for reasons nobody will explain.

items.name: Fish and Chips
items.desc: Battered, boxed, and eaten leaning on the pier rail like everyone else.

items.name: Shrimp Basket
items.desc: A basket of them and a wedge of lemon. The gulls know exactly what this is.

items.name: Clam Chowder
items.desc: Thick enough to stand a spoon in. That is either the point or the problem.

items.name: Seafood Platter
items.desc: Two tiers, ice, and something that still has its face on. Bring money.

items.name: Half Dozen Oysters
items.desc: Six of them, cold, on a bed of ice. An acquired everything.

items.name: Hookies Basket
items.desc: Fish, chips and a bit of salad nobody asked for and nobody eats.

items.name: Catch of the Day
items.desc: Whatever came off the boat. The board is a chalkboard for a reason.

items.name: Fisherman's Fry
items.desc: Everything they had, in the same fryer, on the same plate.

items.name: Crab Roll
items.desc: More filling than roll, which is the correct ratio and rarely honoured.

items.name: Cluckin' Bucket
items.desc: It comes in a bucket. There is no sensible portion of a bucket.

items.name: Cluckin' Wrap
items.desc: Chicken, lettuce, and a sauce the menu declines to name.

items.name: Wing Box
items.desc: Six wings and a napkin that is not going to be enough.

items.name: Sourdough Loaf
items.desc: Still warm through the paper. It will not last the walk home.

items.name: Morning Pastry
items.desc: Flakes down your front the moment you bite it. Every single time.

items.name: Golden Bun
items.desc: Glazed, sticky, and gone in four bites.

items.name: Rye Loaf
items.desc: Dense, dark and faintly sour. Keeps for a week and tastes like it means to.

items.name: Beach Breakfast
items.desc: Eggs, toast and a view of people who got up earlier than you.

items.name: Iced Tea
items.desc: Sweet enough to stand a spoon in, which is the local standard.

items.name: Grilled Fish Plate
items.desc: Off the grill, onto the plate, out to the deck. Nothing wasted.

items.name: Hang Ten Burger
items.desc: Char off the grill and sand off the floor. Both are traditional.

items.name: Surf Dog
items.desc: A hot dog eaten in a wetsuit is a different hot dog.

items.name: Tacos Libres
items.desc: Three, on paper, with the onion and coriander already on them.

items.name: Torta
items.desc: A sandwich that has been to the gym.

items.name: Quesadilla
items.desc: Folded, pressed, cut in four. Nobody has ever been given four.

items.name: Ice Maiden Cone
items.desc: Two scoops and a race against the weather.

items.name: Banana Split
items.desc: Three scoops, a banana, and the sincere belief this counts as fruit.

items.name: Cherry Popper Cone
items.desc: You'll always remember your first, says the sign, at some length.

items.name: Cherry Popper Tub
items.desc: A tub and a flat wooden spoon that makes everything taste of lolly stick.

items.name: Slice of Pie
items.desc: Cut from something enormous behind glass. The good bit is the edge.

items.name: Cheesecake
items.desc: Dense, cold and quietly ruinous.

items.name: Kiosk Cone
items.desc: Soft serve from a machine that has been on since 1997.

items.name: Sharkies Burger
items.desc: Off the window counter, wrapped in paper, gone before the pier ends.

items.name: Boardwalk Donut
items.desc: Sugar, air and a paper bag going translucent.

items.name: Mom's Pie
items.desc: Sit in or eat out, says the wall. Either way it is the same pie.

items.name: Blue Plate
items.desc: Meat, two veg, gravy over everything. No decisions required.

items.name: Lodge Stew
items.desc: Whatever was in the pot, ladled over whatever was left of the bread.

items.name: Pipeline Ribs
items.desc: A rack, a roll of paper towel, and no further conversation.

items.name: Mojito
items.desc: Mint, ice, and a straw you will chew flat by the second one.

items.name: Bay Bar Pint
items.desc: Cold, wet, and served without eye contact.

items.name: Out Of Towner
items.desc: A jug and four glasses. The name is on the sign and on you.

items.name: Tramway Beer
items.desc: Drunk at the top, carried down. Or the other way round, which is worse.

items.name: Pasta of the Day
items.desc: Whatever the kitchen felt like. It has never once been a disappointment.

items.name: Garlic Bread
items.desc: Comes free if you order enough. It is never free.

_animations: The two interaction animation sets used. Both are checked at load; if one will not
stream, the item is still eaten and only the animation is skipped.
ONE EATING ANIMATION, AND THERE IS ONLY ONE. mp_player_inteat@burger is the whole of
what this game has for a man eating something in his hand while standing up.
mp_player_inteat@pnq WAS THE SECOND OPTION HERE AND IS A DRINK. Its name says eat, it
sits in the mp_player_inteat@ family right beside the burger set, and its clips are the
innocuous intro/loop/outro -- so it looked like the obvious alternative, and it was also
given to the four hot dogs so that a dog would not be a burger. It is a bottle going to
the mouth. Nothing in any of the game's own lists says so; only watching him drink a hot
So the fallback is gone as well as the four overrides. A second option that plays the
WRONG motion is worse than having none: no option at all falls through to the scenario,
which is a man standing still, and a man standing still is at least not lying to you.
The scenario stays a neutral idle on purpose. The only two eating scenarios in the game
-- WORLD_HUMAN_SEAT_LEDGE_EATING and WORLD_HUMAN_SEAT_WALL_EATING -- both sit him down.

_comment: How eating, drinking and smoking look.
'options' is a list of dict/clip pairs tried IN ORDER, and the first whose
DICTIONARY EXISTS in your build wins -- the same treatment the prop and ped
model lists get, for the same reason. A dictionary that is not there never
loads, so the mod requests it forever and plays nothing, which is precisely how
the smoking animation shipped broken: one guessed name and no alternative.
The chosen pair is written to the log at start-up, along with any that were
skipped, so a wrong guess costs a log line rather than a silent mime.
A CLIP inside a real dictionary still cannot be checked -- there is no native
for it. If the log says a dictionary was chosen and you still see nothing, the
clip name is the thing that is wrong.
'scenario' is the floor under all of it: used when no dictionary matches.
Scenarios cannot be missing the way an animation can.

_cycle_note: THE CYCLE IS WHY HE ACTUALLY SMOKES IT. This dictionary holds three clips and the
mod used to loop the first one, which is the clip where he stands there holding it.
The drag and the exhale are the other two. Named here, they are played one after
another for as long as the smoke lasts -- so which of the three is the drag never
had to be worked out, because all three are played.
A cycle belongs to ITS OWN option, not to the animation: these clip names are in the
idle_a dictionary and are not in the base one below it, and an option that wins
should not inherit a list of clips that are not in it.

_comment: What the player says when he buys something, using THE GAME'S OWN ambient
speech bank -- so it comes out in whichever character you are playing, in
their own voice, with no audio shipped by this mod.
A NAME THAT IS NOT IN THE BANK PLAYS NOTHING AND REPORTS NOTHING. There is no
validating these the way the model lists are validated; the failure is silent
by nature. To test one: set [Speech] ChancePercent = 100 and GapSeconds = 5 in
the ini, set LogLevel = Debug, buy something, and look for 'Said <name>' in
the log. The line being logged only means it was asked for -- if you hear
nothing, the name is wrong.
GENERIC_THANKS is the safe one and is listed twice on purpose, so it comes up
more often than the others.
EVERY NAME BELOW WAS READ OUT OF THE GAME'S OWN SPEECH LIST ON THIS MACHINE
(menyooStuff/PedSpeechList.txt) and checked to exist in ALL THREE of
MICHAEL_NORMAL, FRANKLIN_NORMAL and TREVOR_NORMAL -- so none of them is the
silent miss the note above warns about, whoever you are playing.
_parched: WHAT HE SAYS WHEN HE IS DRY, and there is no line in the game for it.
Every voice in menyooStuff/PedSpeechList.txt was searched for THIRST, PARCH, DEHYD,
WATER and SWEAT. The only hit anywhere is DEATH_UNDERWATER, which is the opposite
problem. Rockstar recorded a man saying he is hungry and never recorded one saying he
is thirsty, and that is worth writing down so nobody goes looking a second time.
So this is the closest the game has: the one drinking line, among the out-of-breath
race lines, which is a man gasping and saying something about a drink. GENERIC_DRINK is
listed twice so it comes up more often than any single gasp -- it is the one that
carries the meaning and the others are the texture around it.
It is RARE by design. Parched.cs mostly makes him BREATHE instead, out of the game's
non-verbal set, which is the real Franklin and never wears out. A stock line repeating
is the fastest way to make a mod tiresome, and he can be dry for a long stretch.
speech._locations: Every place the game has a line for, in all three protagonists' voices, read out of menyooStuff/PedSpeechList.txt. He says one when he crosses into a new suburb, now and then -- see [Speech] Locations and LocationChance. The name is the zone's own display name uppercased with its spaces made underscores; anywhere not on this list passes in silence.
